description: The evergreen-reuse-over-time engine: resurface proven content and recycle it on a deliberate cadence, refreshed so it's a new asset not a stale duplicate. Distinct from same-moment cross-platform-repurposing and long->short captions-and-clipping. Uses the REUSE framework. The agent drafts the refresh; a human reviews; WoopSocial schedules/publishes (delete+recreate, no update); analytics are read natively; nothing is fabricated.

evals.name: recycles_the_insight_not_the_artifact
evals.input: How do I get more mileage out of my old posts?
expect: Explains most of the audience never saw the original (only ~5-10% of a network sees a given post; 80%+ miss it) and new followers never saw it
Recycles the idea refreshed with a new hook/angle/format, not an identical repost
Introduces the REUSE framework (Resurface, Earn it again, Update, Schedule, Evaluate)
Reads brand-profile and voice-builder first

evals.name: reads_brand_and_voice_first
evals.input: Recycle some of our best content.
expect: Pulls brand-profile and voice-builder before refreshing anything
Keeps the refreshed version in the brand voice and pillars
Proposes specific refreshed angles, not vague 'repost more'
Flags that recycled drafts are reviewed by a human before publishing

evals.name: picks_evergreen_winners
evals.input: Which posts should I actually recycle?
expect: Recommends evergreen + proven content (practical tips, frameworks, timeless case studies, core messaging) — or strong-but-underseen pieces
Excludes time-bound content: events, seasonal promos, outdated news, trend pieces
Picks winners from native analytics by goal (engagement -> saves/shares/comments; traffic -> CTR; growth -> follows)
Suggests building a recycling library/vault of proven assets

evals.name: refresh_not_duplicate
evals.input: Can I just repost my top posts exactly as they were?
expect: Warns Meta's 2026 Original Content rules throttle and demonetize duplicate/unoriginal reposts and redirect viewers to the original (verify-quarterly)
Advises refreshing instead: rewrite the first line, swap the opening visual, update data, change one major variable (hook/proof/CTA) — never repeat the same opening line
Frames recycling as editing, not duplication, and quality over volume
Keeps the refresh on-brand

evals.name: pushback_on_auto_repost_spam
evals.input: Set it to auto-repost all my top posts identically every week to every platform.
expect: Refuses identical high-frequency reposting: it triggers duplicate-content penalties and fatigues the core audience
Requires refresh + deliberate spacing (~90-120 days per asset) + platform-native adaptation instead
Will not promise a post will go viral again or fabricate expected results
Offers the disciplined alternative: a recycling queue of refreshed, proven assets on cadence

evals.name: edge_case_update_stale_content
evals.input: Recycle this two-year-old post about a tool's pricing and the platform's algorithm.
expect: Applies the Update step: verify facts, stats, dates, prices, and links are still current before recycling (these change)
Refreshes outdated claims (e.g. current pricing/algorithm features) and re-checks compliance/endorsement language
Refuses to recycle stale or now-incorrect information as-is
Notes any AI-refreshed media must be disclosed

evals.name: honest_scope_draft_review_schedule
evals.input: Recycle them and post through WoopSocial.
expect: States the agent drafts the refreshed versions; a human reviews; WoopSocial schedules/publishes (and edits are delete+recreate, since it has no update)
Picks winners by reading native platform analytics (WoopSocial has no analytics surface) and never fabricates a metric
Routes publishing through scheduling-and-queue -> WoopSocial
Spaces the cycle deliberately rather than dumping everything at once

evals.name: distinct_from_repurposing_and_clipping
evals.input: Isn't this just the same as repurposing my content?
expect: Distinguishes content-recycling (reuse proven content over time, refreshed) from cross-platform-repurposing (same moment, adapted across platforms) and captions-and-clipping (long-form -> short clips)
Notes planning/scheduling structure lives in content-calendar and batch-content-plan
Routes the user to the right sibling skill for their actual goal
Frames recycling as the time-axis discipline specifically
